claims.text: Selective laser sintering can introduce controlled porosity into HfMoTaTiZr.
Introducing controlled porosity by selective laser sintering can reduce the density of HfMoTaTiZr.
Porous HfMoTaTiZr can retain its mechanical properties at room temperature.
Porous HfMoTaTiZr can retain its mechanical properties at elevated temperatures up to 1000 °C.
Pore size and pore distribution are the structural mediators governing the proposed response.
Selective laser sintering will preserve the high-entropy alloy's grain structure.
Selective laser sintering will preserve the high-entropy alloy's composition.
Preservation of grain structure and composition will allow strength to be maintained despite controlled porosity.
The proposed intervention will produce maintained or slightly reduced strength relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
The proposed performance boundary is room temperature through 1000 °C under tensile and compressive loading.
The optimal pore size and distribution for maintaining mechanical properties are unknown.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says mechanical properties will not be sacrificed, whereas the predicted outcome permits slightly reduced strength.
The no-sacrifice claim is operationalized inconsistently: the rejection rule allows strength losses of up to 20% without falsifying the hypothesis.
